rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal or live-demo instruction anywhere in this file; it is a closing narrative, not a demo beat.

All three body chunks carry a self-standing claim: chunk 1 (186w) the training's rules were built from specific corrected failures; chunk 2 (154w) the testing stack catches differing failure modes; chunk 3 (68w) the student just ran the same compound loop. None is a wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Each header is a true summary of its chunk's content under a sequential read: 'Everything starts as a few bulletpoints somewhere' (chunk describes the strategy-doc-to-rules origin), 'Then we tested the training' (chunk describes judges/simulation/tmux runner), 'You just ran the same loop' (chunk names the student's own just-completed M1 loop). No header contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked all sub-items per chunk: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere. Closest anaphora candidate line 11 'Some were too broad. Some fired in the wrong place.' is a pair, not a triple, so it doesn't trip the third-leg-empty test. No self-grading superlatives (no 'most useful'/'one of the best' phrasing). Number-with-caveat candidate line 13 '302 active rules and subrules across 12 checklists, written over 1,447 commits. Neither count is a claim that more rules make better work' is not the banned shape (a number retracting its own accuracy) — it states the count plainly and then bounds what inference the count licenses, which is a different move than 'about 10%... could be more, could be less'. No abstraction-noun stacks (no 'bounded-window reality' style phrasing); vocabulary throughout is concrete (rules, checklists, commits, judges, simulations, tmux runner). Verb triplet at line 27 'found the useful wrongness, corrected it, and wrote what the session taught you' — all three verbs answer 'what does this concretely mean' on their own (found/corrected/wrote), no empty leg.
